text: SAULT STE. MARIE, Nov. 21, 1912 - All hope has been given up for the wooden package freighter Merriam Grey, which left Port Arthur on Monday with a cargo of flour and has not been heard of since. Wreckage bearing her name, including a lifeboat stove in at the bow and a quantity of floating barrels, was picked up yesterday by the fish tug Ellen off Michipicoten Island. She carried a crew of nineteen, most of them from Collingwood and Owen Sound. Masters arriving here report that the northwest gale on Tuesday night was the worst of the season, and it is believed the Grey, heavily laden and low in the water, foundered in the open lake.

text: Float plane accident, Lac Seul, 2009: a Beaver flipped on its back during a crosswind takeoff. Pilot and two anglers rescued from the floats; one passenger drowned.
label: transport

text: An eastbound passenger train struck a farm truck carrying eleven harvest hands at an unguarded level crossing west of Portage la Prairie on the evening of August 28, 1953. Four of the men were killed outright and the rest were thrown into the ditch. The engineer said the truck drove onto the track without stopping and he had no chance to brake.
label: transport

text: A chartered coach carrying a seniors' group from Kamloops left Highway 5 north of Clearwater on 14 January 2004 and rolled down a snow-covered embankment toward the North Thompson River. The driver told police the rear wheels lost traction on black ice in a curve. Two passengers died at the scene and 23 were taken to hospitals in Clearwater and Kamloops, several with spinal injuries. Rescuers had to cut through the roof to reach people pinned under seats. The coroner later recommended seat belts on all highway coaches.
label: transport

text: Schooner Lillian M. lost with all hands off Cape Sable, December 1909. Seven men, all of Shelburne.
label: transport

text: A twin-engine charter aircraft carrying mining men from Edmonton to Yellowknife crashed into a wooded ridge about 30 miles short of its destination on the afternoon of October 9, 1951. A search plane spotted the wreckage two days later, and a ground party reached it on snowshoes. Of the twelve aboard, only the co-pilot and one passenger were alive; both had spent two nights in the wreck with broken limbs. Investigators believe the pilot descended too early in low cloud.

text: Shortly after 7 a.m. on 18 November 2011, thick fog caused a chain-reaction pileup involving about 40 vehicles in the southbound lanes of Highway 400 north of Barrie. Tractor-trailers jackknifed and several cars were crushed between them; one driver died and 27 people were injured. The highway was closed for twelve hours while police reconstructed the crash.

text: OTTAWA, Sept. 16, 1904 - A heavily laden Bank Street car jumped the rails at the foot of the hill this evening and overturned against a telephone pole. The motorman says the brakes failed to hold on the wet grade. Eighteen passengers were injured, three of them seriously, and were taken to the General and St. Luke's hospitals.
label: transport

text: A survey crew of three was killed in July 1974 when their helicopter struck a ridge in cloud in the Rockies near Golden.
label: transport

text: Shortly before midnight on 11 August 1995, a car ferry running between the mainland and a Bay of Fundy island ran aground on a ledge in dense fog about a kilometre from the terminal. The hull was holed in two compartments and the vessel took on a list of ten degrees. The 140 passengers were mustered on deck in life jackets and taken off by lifeboats and fishing boats that came out from the island harbour. No one was injured. The ferry was refloated on the next high tide and towed to Saint John for repairs, and the service was replaced by a chartered vessel for six weeks. The investigation found that the radar had been malfunctioning since the previous trip.
label: transport

text: CHAPLEAU, Ont., Feb. 2, 1907 - A head-on collision between a westbound passenger train and an eastbound freight occurred at a curve about four miles west of here early this morning, in a blinding snowstorm. The engineer and fireman of the passenger were killed, and the baggage car and first coach were telescoped. Nine passengers, mostly immigrants on their way to the West, were taken from the wreckage alive, though several are badly hurt. A relief train with doctors arrived from White River at noon. It is said that the freight crew misread their orders.
label: transport

text: The Lunenburg trawler Marion Beck capsized and sank on the Grand Banks on February 7, 1959, after freezing spray built a thick coat of ice on her rigging and deck. A sister ship picked up four survivors from a dory after six hours; fifteen men were lost.
label: transport

text: Fuel truck broke through the winter road on Great Bear Lake, March 2006. The driver climbed out the window; the tanker sank with 30,000 litres of diesel.
label: transport

text: WHITEHORSE, Y.T., June 1906 - The sternwheeler Klondike Belle, bound down river for Dawson with forty passengers and a full freight, struck a rock in Five Finger Rapids yesterday and sank in shallow water near the right bank. All aboard got ashore safely, but a large part of the cargo is lost.
label: transport

text: Thirty-one cars of a westbound grain train left the track on a curve east of Hornepayne in the early morning of June 3, 1965, piling up in a cut and spilling wheat across both rails. The head-end crew escaped injury. Investigators found a broken rail where the first car derailed. Wreck crews and two big hook cranes from Capreol worked for three days to clear the line, and transcontinental passenger trains were detoured via the southern route in the meantime. The railway put the loss of grain at about 60,000 bushels.
label: transport

text: A turboprop with 34 people aboard overran the end of the runway while landing in heavy snow at Sault Ste. Marie on 3 February 2002 and came to rest in a snowbank with its nose gear collapsed. Passengers left by the emergency slides; four had minor injuries. Investigators found the runway had not been cleared since the last plough an hour earlier.
label: transport

text: A ferry scow turned over at the Fort Saskatchewan crossing in May 1910, drowning a teamster and his horses.
label: transport

text: A school bus slid off an icy gravel road and overturned in the ditch near Hanna, Alberta, on the morning of December 6, 1961. The driver and 27 children were tossed about inside; eight pupils went to hospital with cuts and broken bones. Farmers nearby used tractors to right the bus.
label: transport

text: Collision report, Trans-Canada Highway east of Kenora, 26 September 2010. At about 14:20 a westbound tanker truck carrying 40,000 litres of gasoline crossed the centre line on a rock-cut curve and struck an eastbound pickup head-on. The tanker rolled and caught fire, and the flames spread to the bush along the shoulder. Both drivers were killed. Kenora fire crews and an OPP unit closed the highway in both directions for 19 hours. Ministry of the Environment staff supervised the recovery of the spilled fuel from the ditch.
label: transport

text: VANCOUVER, May 14, 1914 - The tug Brave capsized in the Fraser River off New Westminster this afternoon while towing a boom of logs against the freshet, and three of her crew of five were drowned. The engineer and a deckhand clung to the floating logs and were rescued by a fish boat.
label: transport

text: Two airmen died near Dauphin, Manitoba, in 1942 when their Harvard trainer spun in during a practice flight.
label: transport

text: A VIA passenger train travelling at about 140 km/h struck a loaded gravel truck that had stalled on a level crossing near Brockville at 9:05 a.m. on 22 May 2001. The locomotive and two coaches derailed but stayed upright. The truck driver jumped clear moments before impact, but the locomotive engineer was killed and 46 passengers were hurt, most of them by flying luggage. The Transportation Safety Board recommended warning lights and gates for the crossing.
label: transport

text: KENORA, Ont., Aug. 4, 1905 - The excursion steamer Lady Gray, with nearly eighty passengers aboard for an afternoon run among the islands of the Lake of the Woods, took fire in the engine room shortly after leaving the wharf. Her master ran her ashore on a sandy point, and the passengers jumped into waist-deep water. A woman and a little boy are missing and believed drowned. The steamer burned to the water line.
label: transport

text: Two lake freighters collided in dense fog in the St. Lawrence channel off Morrisburg on the morning of September 30, 1950. The upbound vessel, loaded with iron ore, was struck amidships and sank in fifteen minutes in 60 feet of water. Her crew of 22 abandoned ship in the lifeboats; a wheelsman is missing.
label: transport

text: Medevac aircraft crash near Lynn Lake, 1998. Two pilots and a flight nurse killed on approach in darkness.
label: transport

text: FERNIE, B.C., Jan. 1908 - A runaway coal train broke loose on the mountain grade above Coal Creek this morning and plunged off a trestle into the creek bed. The brakeman jumped and was injured; the engineer was killed. Sixteen loaded cars are piled in the gully.
label: transport

text: A sudden squall capsized a crowded tour boat among the Thousand Islands below Gananoque on Sunday afternoon, July 24, 1955. The vessel, with 41 people aboard, was rolled over by a gust as she turned in a narrow channel. Cottagers in rowboats and outboards pulled most of the passengers from the water within minutes, but five people, including two small children, were drowned. Witnesses said the boat had been carrying more people than its licence allowed. The Department of Transport opened an inquiry the next day.
label: transport

text: A GO Transit train struck a dump truck that had been stopped on the crossing by traffic in Pickering, Ontario, on 2 March 2006. The truck was split in two and its driver was seriously injured; three train passengers were treated for minor injuries.
label: transport

text: CLINTON, B.C., Oct. 1903 - The down stage went over the bank on the Cariboo Road a few miles north of here; two passengers killed.
label: transport

text: Search and rescue summary: at 04:55 on 9 October 2017 the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre in Halifax received a distress beacon signal from a 15-metre fishing vessel about 60 nautical miles east of St. Anthony, Newfoundland. A Cormorant helicopter and a Coast Guard cutter were tasked. On arrival the helicopter crew found the vessel capsized and three crew members in survival suits clinging to the overturned hull in two-metre seas; a fourth crew member was in a life raft. All four were hoisted aboard and flown to St. Anthony with hypothermia. The vessel had been loading crab pots when it took a heavy roll and did not recover.
label: transport
